findings.title: The signal filter infrastructure the description says was removed is still added to CloudExporter.
findings.body: The description says the "signal filter infrastructure" was removed from this PR. The diff still adds a public `signalFilters` config with per-signal callbacks for spans, logs, metrics, scores and feedback, and wires it into every `on*Event` handler. The new public API also has a side effect: setting `signalFilters.spans` replaces the default filter completely, so the `MODEL_CHUNK` drop this PR is meant to add stops applying. Drop `signalFilters` here and hardcode the `MODEL_CHUNK` check.

findings.title: The `metrics.autoExtract` control is still added despite the description saying it was removed.
findings.body: The description says the "metrics auto-extract controls" were removed. The diff still adds `metrics.autoExtract` to the config types (in both core and observability), to the zod schema and to the instance. Setting it to `false` skips every auto-extracted duration and token metric. The request does not ask for this. Remove it from this PR.

findings.title: Processor observability controls are still in the PR although the description says they were removed.
findings.body: The PR description says it was narrowed to two changes (dropping `MODEL_CHUNK` spans in CloudExporter and a `warn` log default), and that "the processor observability work" was removed and deferred. The diff still adds the public `Processor.observability` option. It also rewires span creation in runner.ts and in both workflow.ts files, and adds the `processorObservability`/`processorOutcome` span attributes. The changeset (`.changeset/observability-volume-controls.md`) also announces these controls. This changes the public API and shared processor code that nobody asked for. Remove it, or update the scope of the request.

findings.title: TripWire processor spans are no longer marked as errors for any processor.
findings.body: Before this change, a TripWire abort in the legacy runner called `processorSpan.error({ error, endSpan: true, ... })`. The removed comment said this was done "so it shows as ERROR in traces". `endTripWireProcessorSpan` now calls `span.end()` with attributes only, so every processor that trips (not just `errors-only` ones) ends as a successful span with no `errorInfo`. Trace UIs, error filters and error-based alerts will stop showing guardrail blocks as errors. This also contradicts the narrowed PR, which claims no processor changes. Keep `span.error({ error, endSpan: true, attributes: getTripWireSpanAttributes(error) })` on the TripWire path, or drop this change from the PR.

findings.title: Dropping successful `errors-only` processor spans leaves their child spans pointing to a parent that was never exported.
findings.body: Processors marked `errors-only` still create a `PROCESSOR_RUN` span, and processor-internal work (for example, nested agent or model calls) is parented under it via `createProcessorObservabilityContext`. CloudExporter drops that span when it succeeds, but its child spans are still exported, and their `parentSpanId` points to a span cloud never receives. Traces in the cloud UI will then show orphaned subtrees. Either drop the descendants as well, or reparent them to the processor span's parent before export. I could not check whether the cloud backend tolerates missing parents.

findings.title: The changeset announces processor controls that the PR says it does not ship.
findings.body: The changeset advertises "controls to run processors without `PROCESSOR_RUN` spans and mark processor spans as errors-only". That contradicts the narrowed scope in the description, and it says nothing about the change in the default log level to `warn`, which affects users. Make the changeset match what actually ships.
